sn1.29:1.1: These verses, with a brief setting, are also at [sn2.28:2.1](). | The “four wheels” of a cart are compared to the body, but the application of the metaphor is not obvious. The commentary relates it to the four postures. Later Buddhist tantra speaks of four “wheels” (_cakra_) in the sense of dynamic centers of vital and spiritual energy—navel, heart, throat, crown. This is attested much later than the suttas, but this could be a precedent. | The “nine doors” are the nine apertures of the body (compare the eleven doors at [mn52:15.5]()).
sn1.29:1.4: The phrase _yātrā bhavissati_ is familiar from the mendicant’s reflection on eating only so that they “will keep going”. The problem here is that the body is bound up with suffering.
